A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DECS research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original seven-benchmark evaluations, component ablations, training diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Qwen3-4B evaluations, detector reliability assessments, and reward-sign diagnostics.

M1.justification: Equation 9 changes correct redundant-token rewards from r0 + (r+ - r0)/Li to r0 - (r+ - r0)Li/Lmax. This is a localized algorithmic revision; NRP detection, advantage normalization, and curriculum scheduling remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both retain DeepScaleR, OpenR1-Math-220K, and the same seven evaluation benchmarks. The detector audit examines science and coding inputs already represented in v1's evaluations and NRP case studies. Qwen3 expands model configurations without introducing new task coverage.

E2.justification: New Figure 9c adds GRPO to the DS-1.5B Pass@K comparison, which previously compared only Base and DECS in Figure 3c. Comparator membership in the main and supplementary benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds the Qwen3-4B configuration, checkpoint-based reward diagnostics, and an audit by three independent experts covering 100 correct responses from each of GPQA-Diamond and LiveCodeBench. Existing benchmark metrics, rollout counts, decoding settings, and original training hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C/Table 5 newly checks whether leading redundant tokens receive positive advantages during training. Appendix G.6/Table 6 directly tests detector reliability outside mathematics. Backbone generalization and new reward-assignment/token-entropy examples further expand validation of central mechanism and transfer assumptions. Earlier ablations and sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-training-seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The existing sampling and Pass@K estimation practices remain; the new annotator-specific accuracies are separate evaluation outcomes.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports Qwen3-4B accuracy increasing from 68.40 to 69.72 and average tokens decreasing from 9,104 to 4,115 with DECS. Table 6 adds detector accuracies of 98.96–99.23% on GPQA-D and 97.49–97.88% on LiveCodeBench. Table 5 reports zero positive-advantage cases at valid checkpoints, and Figure 9c adds GRPO curves. Original numerical tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix C supplies a case-based derivation for negative leading-redundant-token advantages, using an assumption linking sequence-length and NRP-length ordering. Its longest-NRP case receives empirical support. This supplements one reward property; the original lemmas, theorems, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: two flaws in sequence-level length rewards, their mitigation through decoupled rewards and curriculum scheduling, and substantial token reduction while preserving reasoning performance.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of backbone robustness and detector reliability as support for transfer, and explains the mechanism through structured credit assignment and relative overgeneralization. The original limitations concerning detector overhead and evaluation only up to 7B are retained, moving from Appendix C to E.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a DECS code-repository address, supplementing v1's statement that code would accompany supplementary materials. Existing hardware information, training hyperparameter tables, detector training recipe, and evaluation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix D positions the method relative to multi-agent RL's relative overgeneralization and structured credit assignment. The existing related-work section is unchanged. The additional Yang et al. Qwen3 entry refers to a work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds targeted explanations, a backbone-generalization subsection, and two appendix sections, while updating terminology, author notes, publication headers, and acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is revised around a worked example; Tables 2 and 4–6 and Figures 11–12 are added; Figures 7 and 9 gain panels. Figure 7c redisplays existing benchmark results, whereas Figure 9c adds a comparison. The original three case-study figures are retained as Figures 13–15.

improvement.justification: The Qwen3 experiment, human detector audit, and reward-sign checks strengthen support for generalization and mechanism reliability. Worked examples and code-access information also improve usability. These gains are tempered by incomplete reward documentation: Section 4.2 still describes the revised reward as inverse-proportional, and Appendix C offers conditional and empirical support rather than an unconditional guarantee.
